extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A dataset consisting of 7,787 natural science questions (authored for standardized tests) partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The Challenge Set contains questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm, requiring advanced reasoning beyond surface-level cues. The dataset includes a corpus of 14M science-related sentences (ARC Corpus) and baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, DGEM).
extraction.creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv preprint arXiv:1803.05457.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7,787 natural science questions drawn from a variety of standardized test sources (e.g., MCAS, TIMSS, NY Regents) and partitioned into Challenge and Easy Sets based on performance of retrieval and co-occurrence baselines. The ARC Corpus (14M science-related sentences) was collected via automated search queries over science topics and augmented with existing corpora (e.g., AristoMini).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Standardized science test questions (e.g., MCAS, TIMSS, NY Regents) and science-related sentences mined from the Web via search engine queries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Questions were collected over several months of extensive search and investigation prior to 2018. The ARC Corpus was constructed using automated search queries relevant to science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to exclude diagram-based questions and standardized into a multiple-choice format. The ARC Corpus was deduplicated, stripped of non-text content, and chunked into sentences. Sentences were filtered for noise (e.g., long sentences, negation, non-science relevance).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were authored for standardized tests and reviewed by examiners. No additional human annotation was performed for the dataset itself; annotations were derived from the original test sources.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (for corpus retrieval), Open IE (for structured representation in entailment models), proprietary parsers (for DGEM).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, baseline models, and leaderboard are maintained and accessible via http://data.allenai.org/arc. The dataset is publicly available and includes versioning information for the Challenge and Easy Sets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance AI research in complex question answering requiring reasoning and commonsense knowledge, addressing limitations of prior QA datasets that relied on surface-level cues.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may arise from the source standardized tests (e.g., cultural or regional focus in test design) and the automated corpus collection process (e.g., overrepresentation of certain science topics).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set may not fully capture all forms of advanced reasoning due to its definition based on specific baseline failures. The ARC Corpus, while large, may not cover all necessary knowledge for every question, and simple retrieval methods may not exploit distributed evidence effectively.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for advanced question-answering systems requiring reasoning and commonsense knowledge. The dataset is designed to push AI research beyond factoid-style QA tasks.
